description.narrative: EDEN Center is an Albanian non-governmental environmental organization. This is core support to their Strategic Plan 2023-2028. EDEN Center will focus its work in 4 strategic directions: 1) Public participation in environmental decision-making; 2) Climate Change and Energy; 3) The green economy; 4) Environmental activism and youth. The support will contribute to improving the internal capacities of EDEN including mainstreaming of perspectives.

EDEN Center är en albansk icke-statlig miljöorganisation. Detta är ett centralt stöd för deras strategiska plan 2023-2028. EDEN Center kommer att fokusera sitt arbete i 4 strategiska riktningar: 1) Allmänhetens deltagande i beslutsfattande på miljöområdet; 2) Klimatförändringar och energi. 3) Den gröna ekonomin. 4) Miljöaktivism och ungdomar. Stödet kommer att bidra till att förbättra den interna kapaciteten i EDEN, bland annat genom att integrera olika perspektiv.

The overall objective of EDEN Center Strategy 2023-2028 is that Albania transitions toward climate neutrality and sustainable development through inclusive governance, empowered civil society, and green solutions - built on trust and collaboration among citizens, civil society, and institutions.
The specific objectives are:
1) Public participation and accountability in environmental decision-making is increased through environmental watchdog mechanisms that protect community voices and rights;
2) Energy and climate policies are strengthened through advocacy actions by civil society organizations.
3) Public services are delivered according to green economy principles, supporting sustainable coexistence between people and nature;
4) Environmental activism is increased through education, volunteerism and civic mobilization promoted and nurtured by EDEN.
5) EDEN's internal capacities are strengthened to support effective and sustainable organizational development.

Component 1: Public Participation and Accountability in Environmental Decision-Making: In 2025, EDEN strengthened public participation and accountability in environmental decision-making through participatory processes and policy engagement, contributing to more transparent and inclusive environmental governance in the context of Albania's EU integration. EDEN actively participated in public consultation mechanisms at both central and municipal levels, provided comments on the EU Country Report, and continued its engagement as a member of the Ministry of Environment's consultation platform.
EDEN also contributed to public consultations organized by the Municipality of Tirana on the Draft Local Action Plan for Air Quality Management (2026-2028), including through its #Youth4CleanAir campaign.
A significant achievement was EDEN's selection as a permanent observer in the EU-Albania Civil Society Joint Consultative Committee, a platform comprising representatives from the European Economic and Social Committee (EESC), Albanian social partners, and civil society organizations. EDEN further contributed to the participatory development of the nomination dossier for the Shkoder Lake Watershed UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and maintained its engagement in public consultation processes related to Chapter 27 of the EU acquis.
In 2025, EDEN also became a member of the CEE Bankwatch Network. Through this membership, the organization developed and adopted two national action plans aligned with Bankwatch's regional priorities, focusing on public finance accountability and the right to participate in environmental decision-making.
Component 2: Climate Change and Energy: The revision of Albania's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0) in 2025 represented an important opportunity to align national climate ambitions with EU and regional frameworks, including the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans. EDEN contributed to strengthening climate and energy policymaking by combining national stakeholder engagement with regional advocacy efforts, promoting more ambitious, inclusive, and coordinated climate action. Key contributions included participation in the development of regional civil society policy briefs on NDC 3.0 in the Western Balkans and joint NGO recommendations for the implementation of the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans Action Plan.
Component 3: Green Economy: Through the project "Value What You Keep", EDEN funded and mentored five gender-responsive circular economy initiatives implemented across seven municipalities. The initiative strengthened the capacities of sub-grantees and facilitated cooperation between civil society organizations and local authorities, contributing to improved multi-stakeholder coordination. As an example, the Municipality of Prrenjas expressed its commitment to expand circular economy investments and employment opportunities following the pilot intervention.
EDEN also contributed to the conservation of Pelophylax shqipericus, an endemic amphibian species of the Shkoder Lake ecosystem, through field research and targeted habitat restoration measures. These efforts strengthened biodiversity monitoring, restored critical habitats, and advanced practical conservation actions within the ecosystem.
In addition, EDEN participated in Lead Poisoning Prevention Week 2025 in partnership with the Public Health Institution, contributing to increased awareness and stronger intersectoral cooperation on lead exposure prevention.
Component 4: Environmental Activism and Youth: EDEN promoted youth engagement in environmental and climate governance through a range of national and regional initiatives that facilitated dialogue, learning, networking, and participation in policy processes. Key achievements included: - Organizing the second Youth Climate Summit, "Joint Venture for Climate and Clean Air and Child-Friendly NDCs Ahead of COP30" under the #Youth4CleanAir campaign. -Supporting youth engagement with policymakers, including during the 2025 national elections, when young people presented a youth-led air quality recommendations package to political parties. - Developing the #Feel4Climate Eco-Anxiety Toolbox in collaboration with Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI), providing interactive tools and games that support youth in addressing climate anxiety while fostering resilience and collective action. - Co-organizing a regional workshop with UNESCO on youth engagement in environmental and climate governance in South-East Europe. The workshop strengthened regional cooperation and resulted in the co-development of a joint Regional Youth Perspective for COP30. - Launching "Youth Chronicles by EDEN", a youth-led platform promoting peer-to-peer learning, critical thinking, and local environmental action. Five editions were organized during the year, covering environmental activism, upcycling, youth participation in urban planning, composting solutions, and recomposing methods. - Marking key international observance days, including World Wetlands Day, International Women's Day, World Environment Day, and the International Day Against Pesticide Use, to raise awareness and encourage environmental action.
Component 5: Organizational Capacity Development: Sida's core support represented EDEN's first experience with flexible institutional funding and was subsequently complemented by a EUR 150,000 core support grant from the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation for the period 2026-2028. The transition from project-based management towards strategic planning, results-based reporting, and organizational development has been one of the most significant outcomes of the support.
Core funding has enabled EDEN to strengthen internal systems, improve strategic and outcome-oriented planning, and develop a clearer understanding of its organizational contribution and long-term impact. This has enhanced both internal alignment and external communication of EDEN's role and values.
During 2025, EDEN also strengthened its operational capacity by adopting the Alfa accounting software system for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 and investing in staff capacity development in Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL), gender equality, anti-corruption, and intersectionality. These investments have contributed to improved organizational effectiveness, accountability, and sustainability.
